_note: QUEST DATA (docs/QUESTS.md). The MECHANICS are real; every `lines`, `label` and `journal` string is a PLACEHOLDER the owner rewrites — keep the keys and structure. A quest is a set of STATES; each state has what the giver says (`lines`, optionally per run: {"1": [...], "2": [...]}), what the journal says (`journal`), and the `choices` the player can make. A choice may `need` something ("ammo": N bullets, or "item": id) and `do` a list of effects: take_ammo:N  take_item:ID  give_item:ID  give_gun:PRESET  upgrade:ID  kill:NPC  outcome:NAME  complete  goto:STATE  banner:TEXT  flag:NAME. `world` says what the quest's place looks like in LATER runs, by outcome ("" = never resolved): a list of specs per run — {npc,mood} {body} {zombies} {drop,half,key} {gun,key}.

offer.journal: Johnny, holding his floor with a gun, will trade a good gun for ten bullets.
lines: Hey. You got bullets? Ten of them and I'll make it worth your while.
Ten bullets. That's the price of a proper gun. You in?

paid.journal: Johnny gave you a gun. Twenty more bullets and he'll give you something better.
lines: Told you I'd make it worth it. Bring me twenty more and I'll do more than hand you a gun.
Twenty more. Then I teach you something.
We're square. Don't go getting yourself killed.

offer.journal: Ethel's husband has been bitten. She begs for medicine — or for you to end it.
lines: My husband... he was bitten. Please, have you anything for him? Anything at all?
He's burning up. If there's a cure, a medicine, anything — please.

choices.label: Give her a first aid kit
Put him out of his misery

supplied.journal: You gave Ethel supplies. Whether they were enough, you'll learn later.
lines: Thank you. Thank you. We'll stay right here and hope.

mercy.journal: You put Ethel's husband out of his misery.

2: He's gone. I keep thinking I should have... never mind. Leave me be.
I can't leave him. Not yet.
